summary: This Part II of AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry builds the numerical theory of invertible sheaves on proper schemes and the descent of contractions it controls. NP.0–NP.1 import curve degree and define its relative numerical pairing, relative numerical triviality Pic^τ(X/S), the groups Num(X/S), N¹(X/S), N₁(X/S), the cone NE‾(X/S), relative nefness and bigness, and prove the numerical Néron–Severi theorem. NP.2 extends the Picard theory of the parent and of JacobianChallenge Layer D to arbitrary proper schemes over a field: Murre–Oort representability, the Brauer obstruction over the affinization, Pic^τ_{X/k} of finite type, the étale local system Num_{X/k} and Schröer's positive-power criterion. NP.3–NP.4 prove Schröer's descent theorems: with constant Num, geometric contractions with projective target descend (Theorem 1.3), and for contractions of smooth proper surfaces fibre dual graphs, residue fields and edge labels descend (Theorem 2.1, corrected). NP.5 supplies the general numerical statements the mixed-characteristic MMP papers of Hacon–Witaszek and Bhatt et al. use: restriction to the special fibre over a DVR, numerical versus actual lifts, lifting with H²(O) = 0, cone identification, nef-and-big transfer, descent of semiample numerically trivial sheaves, Cascini–Tanaka vertical descent, extremal curves and the complex projective Alexeev–Hacon–Kawamata rank (its relative positive-characteristic extension remains open). The stable-surface moduli direction routed to the same parent is proposed as a separate roadmap, and the MMP-internal steps are assigned to the birational-geometry continuation of SchemeAndStackFoundations. The review records explicit proof/supplier gaps G1–G7; a complete planning pass does not certify closure of the later layers. All six layers are planned at target level under Protocol section 0, with explicit gap endpoints; none is closed.

nodes.title: Imported curve degree and its relative numerical pairing
nodes.statement: Use the degree of invertible sheaves on proper schemes of dimension at most one owned by StableReduction J-A2 (the JacobianChallenge Layer A contract) and SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.3/vector-bundle-degree. Its convention is deg_κ(L) = χ_κ(C,L) − χ_κ(C,O_C), allowing nonreduced curves and zero-dimensional components. This node identifies that imported degree with SF.5 first-Chern-class intersections and defines only the application (L·C) := deg_{κ(s)}(L|_C) for an integral curve C in X_s. The residue field κ(s) is part of the pairing, even when C has a larger field of constants.
hypotheses: κ a field; C proper over κ of dimension at most one
for (L·C): C is an integral curve in a fibre X_s, proper over κ(s)
proofSteps: Import the Euler-characteristic degree and its tensor, cycle, finite-pullback and field-extension laws from StableReduction J-A2/JacobianChallenge Layer A and SF.3/vector-bundle-degree; coherent finiteness and base change are JacobianChallenge B–C. No second degree theory is constructed here.

Compare the imported degree with SF.5/c1_degree_curve by the degree-one Euler-characteristic intersection formula (Stacks Section 33.45). Tensor additivity and the vanishing contribution from zero-dimensional components are imported laws.

Cycle formula: deg_κ(L) = Σ_i m_i deg_κ(L|_{C_i}) over the one-dimensional irreducible components C_i with reduced structure, m_i = length O_{C,η_i}; zero-dimensional components contribute nothing. This is SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.3's c1_degree_curve, deg(c₁(L) ∩ [C]_1), on the fundamental 1-cycle.

On an integral proper curve the degree equals the degree of the pullback to the normalization and the residue-weighted degree of the divisor of any rational section (JacobianChallenge Layer A, Kleiman 2005, Definition 6.1).
acceptance: deg_κ O_{P¹_κ}(m) = m.
deg over κ depends on κ: P¹_ℂ regarded as an ℝ-scheme has deg_ℝ O(1) = 2.
On the double line V(y²) ⊂ P²_κ, deg O(1)|_C = 2.

nodes.title: Divisibility of curve degrees by the geometric index d_C
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme locally of finite type over a field k, C ⊂ X an integral curve proper over k, k̄ an algebraic closure and φ : X_{k̄} → X the projection. There is an integer d_C ≥ 1, depending only on C, such that for every invertible sheaf L on X (more generally every ℝ-Cartier divisor D) and every integral curve C′ ⊂ X_{k̄} with φ(C′) = C one has (L·C)_k = d_C·(φ*L·C′)_{k̄}. In particular d_C divides (L·C)_k for every invertible L. Explicitly d_C = m·r, where (C_{k̄})_red has r irreducible components, all of multiplicity m in the fundamental cycle of C_{k̄}.
hypotheses: k a field, C integral and proper over k
the conclusion is for every component C′ of (C_{k̄})_red
proofSteps: The group Aut(k̄/k) permutes the irreducible components of C_{k̄} transitively, since C is irreducible and k̄/k is normal (purely inseparable steps are homeomorphisms).
Conjugate components have equal multiplicity in [C_{k̄}] and equal φ*L-degree, because φ*L is Aut(k̄/k)-invariant up to isomorphism.
Field-extension invariance of degrees (curve-degree API) gives (L·C)_k = deg_{k̄}(φ*L|_{C_{k̄}}) = Σ_i m·(φ*L·C′_i) = m·r·(φ*L·C′).

Das–Waldron Lemma 4.1 expresses the same index as [L:k]/[K(E):K(C)], with their finite fields of definition and notation; it is a quotient, not a product. The cycle calculation above supplies the intrinsic integer m·r without choices of fields.
acceptance: For C = P¹_ℂ viewed over ℝ, d_C = 2 and every invertible sheaf has even ℝ-degree on C.
For k = F_p(t), k′ = k(t^{1/p}) and C = P¹_{k′} viewed over k, C_{k̄} is a p-fold thickening of P¹_{k̄}: d_C = p.
For geometrically integral C, d_C = 1.

Lemma 3.6 gives invariance of a curve intersection under extending the ground field; Lemma 4.1, pp. 12–13, gives d_C = [L:k]/[K(E):K(C)] and the common factor relating an integral curve to its geometric components.

nodes.title: Numerical triviality is invariant under extension of the base field
nodes.statement: Let X be proper over a field k, L ∈ Pic(X) and K/k any field extension. Then (L·C) = 0 for every integral curve C ⊂ X if and only if (L_K·C′) = 0 for every integral curve C′ ⊂ X_K.
hypotheses: X proper over k; K/k arbitrary (not necessarily algebraic)
proofSteps: (⇐) For C ⊂ X, the base change C_K is a proper one-dimensional K-scheme and deg_k(L|_C) = deg_K(L_K|_{C_K}) = Σ_i m_i (L_K·C_i) = 0.
(⇒), K/k finite: X_K → X is finite; a curve C′ ⊂ X_K maps finitely onto an integral curve C ⊂ X, and the projection formula gives [K:k]·(L_K·C′)_K = [κ(C′):κ(C)]·(L·C)_k = 0.

(⇒), general K: C′ is defined over a finitely generated k-subalgebra A ⊂ K; spread C′ to a flat proper family of curves over an open of Spec A and specialise to a closed point a, whose residue field is finite over k (Nullstellensatz). Degrees are constant in flat proper families of curves (χ(L^{⊗n}) is locally constant), so (L_K·C′) equals a degree on X_{κ(a)}, which vanishes by the finite case.
Equivalently: the τ-component of the Picard scheme commutes with extension of k and its points are the numerically trivial classes (Kleiman, Proposition 6.12 and Remark 6.14).
acceptance: On P¹_ℝ, O(m) is numerically trivial iff it is so on P¹_ℂ, iff m = 0.
A curve on X_K need not map onto a curve of X (a generic line of P²_{k(u)} dominates P²_k); the proof specialises instead of taking images.

nodes.title: Relative numerical triviality and the subgroup Pic^τ(X/S)
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be a proper morphism with S Noetherian. An invertible sheaf L on X is f-numerically trivial, written L ≡_f 0 (or L ≡_S 0), if (L·C) = 0 for every point s ∈ S and every integral curve C ⊂ X_s. Two invertible sheaves are f-numerically equivalent if L ⊗ M^{-1} ≡_f 0. The f-numerically trivial classes form a subgroup Pic^τ(X/S) ⊂ Pic(X); this subgroup of Pic(X) is distinct from the group scheme Pic^τ_{X/k} of NP.2, whose rational points it is compared with there. For S = Spec k this is numerical equivalence on the proper k-scheme X.
hypotheses: f proper, S Noetherian
curves in all fibres, degrees over residue fields of S
proofSteps: The subgroup property is the tensor and inverse API of NP.0/curve-degree.

By NP.0/closed-points-suffice the condition may be tested over closed points of S only (the convention of Bhatt et al.), and by NP.0/field-extension-invariance on geometric fibres (the convention of Schröer).
acceptance: f*N ≡_f 0 for every N ∈ Pic(S).
For the identity X = S every invertible sheaf is numerically trivial.
On an Enriques surface over k̄ of characteristic ≠ 2, ω is numerically trivial and nontrivial.

nodes.title: Numerical triviality can be tested over closed points of the base
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be proper with S Noetherian and L ∈ Pic(X). If (L·D) = 0 for every closed point t ∈ S and every integral curve D ⊂ X_t, then L ≡_f 0.
hypotheses: f proper, S Noetherian
proofSteps: Suppose the conclusion fails at some point; by Noetherian induction choose a failing point s whose closure T is minimal. T ≠ {s}, since closed points satisfy the hypothesis.

Choose a codimension-one point t′ of T and apply Stacks Lemma 10.119.13 (00PH) to O_{T,t′}. This gives a dominating DVR R with fraction field κ(s); its residue field extends κ(t′), and that extension need not be assumed finite.

For a curve C ⊂ X_s, base change its closure to Spec R and take the flat closure Z of its generic fibre; Z is proper and flat of relative dimension one over R, and χ(L^{⊗n}) is constant on its fibres, so the degree of L on C (with generic ground field κ(s)) equals the degree on the special fibre, a one-dimensional proper scheme over κ(R).

The special fibre's one-dimensional components lie in X_{t′} ⊗ κ(R); L is numerically trivial on X_{t′} by minimality of T, hence on X_{t′} ⊗ κ(R) (NP.0/field-extension-invariance). The cycle formula gives degree 0, a contradiction.
acceptance: Over S = Spec ℤ_p and X = P¹_S, testing the special fibre recovers O(m) ≡_f 0 iff m = 0.

Generic fibres alone do not suffice: let X = Bl_x(P¹_R) for a k-rational point x of the special fibre over a DVR R. The exceptional curve E is P¹_k, O(E) has degree −1 on E, and its restriction to the generic fibre is trivial.

nodes.title: Proper surjective pullback detects numerical triviality
nodes.statement: Let g : X′ → X be a proper surjective morphism of schemes proper over a Noetherian S. For L ∈ Pic(X), L ≡_S 0 if and only if g*L ≡_S 0. Hence g* : Num(X/S) → Num(X′/S) (NP.1) is injective.
hypotheses: g proper and surjective over S; X, X′ proper over S Noetherian
proofSteps: (⇒) A curve C′ in a fibre of X′ maps onto a curve D or to a point; by the projection formula (g*L·C′) = [κ(C′):κ(D)](L·D), or 0.

(⇐) Given a curve D ⊂ X_s, the generic fibre of g over the generic point of D is a nonempty proper scheme; the closure of one of its closed points is an integral curve C′ ⊂ X′_s mapping finitely onto D, and (g*L·C′) = [κ(C′):κ(D)](L·D) with a positive factor.
acceptance: For the normalization ν : C̃ → C of a nodal cubic, ν*L ≡ 0 iff L ≡ 0.

nodes.title: The relative numerical group N¹(X/S) and the relative Picard number
nodes.statement: For f : X → S proper with S Noetherian put Num(X/S) := Pic(X)/Pic^τ(X/S), N¹(X/S)_ℚ := Num(X/S) ⊗ ℚ and N¹(X/S) := N¹(X/S)_ℝ := Num(X/S) ⊗ ℝ, with the class map [−] : Pic(X) → Num(X/S). The relative Picard number is ρ(X/S) := dim_ℝ N¹(X/S), finite by NP.1/finite-dimensionality. Equivalently N¹(X/S)_ℚ is (Pic(X) ⊗ ℚ) modulo the kernel of the ℚ-linear degree pairing with curves in fibres, which is Hacon–Witaszek's N¹(X) = Pic(X) ⊗ ℚ/≡ for S = Spec k.

nodes.title: Numerical Néron–Severi theorem for proper schemes over a field
nodes.statement: Let X be proper over a field k. Then Num(X/k) is a free abelian group of finite rank, and rank Num(X/k) ≤ ρ(X_{k̄}) := rank Num(X_{k̄}/k̄). For k algebraically closed and ℓ a prime invertible in k, ρ(X) ≤ dim_{𝔽_ℓ} H²_ét(X, μ_ℓ).
hypotheses: X proper over a field; the étale bound needs ℓ invertible in k and k algebraically closed
proofSteps: Num(X/k) ↪ Num(X_{k̄}/k̄) (NP.1/numerical-group, base-change API), so assume k = k̄.

Rank bound: if b_1, …, b_r ∈ Num are ℤ-independent, choose curves C_1, …, C_r with det((b_i·C_j)) ≠ 0; the image of Num → ℤ^r, L ↦ ((L·C_j))_j, is a lattice of rank r, so dim_{𝔽_ℓ} Num/ℓNum ≥ r. Num/ℓ is a quotient of Pic(X)/ℓ, which injects into H²_ét(X, μ_ℓ) by the Kummer sequence; that group is finite for X proper over k = k̄. The all-dimensional étale finiteness input has not been located in a registered supplier; it remains gap G1. Kleiman Remark 6.19 records finite generation as a theorem, but does not provide this proof input.
Freeness: with r = rank Num, choose curves with det((b_i·C_j)) ≠ 0 for a ℚ-basis b_i; L ↦ ((L·C_j)) is injective on the torsion-free Num, so Num embeds in ℤ^r.
In characteristic zero this recovers AbundanceStatement Layer 4B item 2 for projective varieties; for smooth projective surfaces it recovers SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.10's Num.free_finiteRank.

nodes.title: Finite-dimensionality of N¹(X/S) over a Noetherian base
nodes.statement: For f : X → S proper with S Noetherian, Num(X/S) is a free abelian group of finite rank, so N¹(X/S) is finite-dimensional and ρ(X/S) < ∞.
hypotheses: f proper, S Noetherian
proofSteps: The absolute result over a field is NP.1/neron-severi-rank, subject to its recorded cohomological supplier gap. Relative finite-dimensionality is a target recorded in BMP23 Remark 2.22; the former generic-flatness sketch does not prove it.

A possible reduction is a projective Chow cover followed by a finite stratification and finite field covers on which each reduced geometric component spreads to a flat geometrically integral projective family. On each such component, Kleiman Theorem 6.3(g) detects numerical triviality by χ(L^p(n)) = χ(O(n)) for every p,n, and these Euler characteristics are constant in a connected flat proper family.

That componentwise reduction, including simultaneous coverage of every fibre and descent of the numerical kernel, is not supplied by generic flatness alone. It is gap G2; no closure is claimed for the general Noetherian-base theorem.

Once the reduction is established, inject the degree quotient into the direct sum of the generic numerical lattices and the numerical quotient on the closed complement, and use Noetherian induction. A subgroup of a finite direct sum of finite free abelian groups is finite free.

nodes.title: Big invertible sheaves on integral proper schemes over a field
nodes.statement: Let V be an integral proper scheme of dimension n over a field k. An invertible sheaf L on V is big if there is c > 0 with h⁰(V, L^{⊗m}) ≥ c·m^n for all sufficiently large and divisible m. Top intersection numbers (L^n·V) are the n-fold numerical intersections of SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.3 / Stacks §33.45. For projective V and nef L, L is big iff (L^n·V) > 0, imported from SF.5/nef-big-numerical. Extending this criterion to arbitrary integral proper V is a remaining target (G3).

proofSteps: Import the reduced projective nef-and-big criterion from SF.5/nef-big-numerical. Keel, Definition–Lemma 0.0, printed p. 254 (PDF p. 2), states this criterion; Lemma 1.7, printed p. 262, is a consequence about the exceptional locus, not its original statement.

Bigness is invariant under numerical equivalence on projective integral schemes, without a nefness assumption. The present proof uses only the imported nef criterion; no unsupported assertion about higher cohomology or Fujita vanishing is made.

The definition makes sense on arbitrary proper integral V, and field-extension invariance follows from flat base change of H⁰. A proof of the nef top-intersection criterion in that broader setting requires proper birational invariance of bigness and a projective Chow modification; this extension is recorded in G3.

nodes.title: The Picard scheme of a proper scheme over a field (Murre–Oort)
nodes.statement: Let X be a proper scheme over a field k, not necessarily reduced, connected or equidimensional, and without assuming H⁰(X, O_X) = k. The fppf sheafification Pic_{X/k} of T ↦ Pic(X_T) on k-schemes (equivalently of T ↦ Pic(X_T)/Pic(T)) is represented by a commutative group scheme, locally of finite type and separated over k, which is a disjoint union of open quasi-projective subschemes. Formation of Pic_{X/k} commutes with every field extension K/k.
hypotheses: X proper over a field; no condition on H⁰(X, O_X), reducedness or connectedness
proofSteps: Kleiman Corollary 4.18.3 states the arbitrary proper-field theorem; Proposition 4.17 proves local finite type. The projective geometrically integral case is imported from JacobianChallenge D and the parent/ComplexComparison Picard contracts.

The extension to arbitrary proper, possibly nonreduced X requires Murre–Oort/Raynaud representability: nilpotent dévissage and nonflat descent along a projective Chow cover. Kleiman Theorem 4.18.5 states relative representability, and pp. 34–35 describe these ingredients, but do not prove them. They remain gap G4.

One cannot handle an arbitrary projective X merely component by component: intersections and nilpotent thickenings carry gluing data. No universal-functions hypothesis is added, and no such false reduction is used.

Given representability, base change follows from the relative Picard sheaf and separatedness from the closed identity of the locally finite-type group scheme over a field. The cited quasi-projective-open decomposition belongs to the representability input.

For X = Spec k[ε]/(ε²), Pic(X_T) = 0 for local T, so Pic_{X/k} is the trivial group scheme although H⁰(X, O_X) ≠ k.

nodes.title: Cohomological Brauer groups of finite algebras over a field are torsion
nodes.statement: Let R be a finite k-algebra and h : Spec R → Spec k. On the small étale sites, h_* is exact and R^i h_*G_m = 0 for every i > 0. Thus the Leray edge H²_et(k,h_*G_m) → H²_et(R,G_m) is an isomorphism. Comparison with fppf cohomology for the smooth units group identifies this with H²_fppf(k,h_*G_m) ≅ H²_fppf(R,G_m). Nilpotent invariance identifies the latter with ⊕_i Br(K_i), where R_red = ∏_i K_i; it is torsion. The corresponding degree-one comparison is zero because Pic(R) = 0.
hypotheses: R finite over a field k; cohomology is étale (= fppf) cohomology with G_m coefficients
proofSteps: Import SF.2/finite-pushforward-exact on small étale sites, for all abelian sheaves and without a torsion restriction. This yields the Leray isomorphisms in degrees one and two directly.

For fppf comparison, the Weil restriction h_*G_m is a smooth affine group scheme: it is the open units locus in the affine space of the finite-dimensional k-algebra R. Use the smooth-group étale/fppf comparison stated in Kleiman Remark 2.11, p. 21. No exactness of arbitrary finite fppf pushforward is assumed.

For a nilpotent ideal I, filter 1+I by the groups 1+I^j; the successive quotients are additive quasi-coherent modules and have no higher cohomology on affine Spec R. This gives nilpotent invariance of H²(G_m).
A finite reduced k-algebra is a product of fields. Their Brauer groups are torsion by SF.2 field cohomology/Brauer comparison. Pic(R) = 0 is the pinned semilocal CommRing.Pic instance.

nodes.statement: Let h : X → Spec k be proper. The fppf Leray spectral sequence for h and G_m gives an exact sequence 0 → Pic(X) → Pic_{X/k}(k) → H²(k, h_*G_m) ≅ Br(X^aff) → H²(X, G_m), with the first map the canonical one. Since Br(X^aff) is torsion, for every λ ∈ Pic_{X/k}(k) there is n ≥ 1 with n·λ the class of an invertible sheaf on X. For every field K ⊃ k the map Pic(X_K) → Pic_{X/k}(K) is injective.
hypotheses: X proper over a field; H⁰(X, O_X) arbitrary
proofSteps: R¹h_*G_m is the fppf Picard sheaf Pic_{X/k} (Hilbert 90, SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.11), and h_*G_m = (X^aff → Spec k)_*G_m (NP.2/affinization).
The five-term sequence 0 → H¹(k, h_*G_m) → H¹(X, G_m) → H⁰(k, R¹h_*G_m) → H²(k, h_*G_m) → H²(X, G_m) has H¹(k, h_*G_m) = Pic(X^aff) = 0 (NP.2/finite-algebra-brauer, i = 1).
H²(k, h_*G_m) ≅ Br(X^aff) is torsion by NP.2/finite-algebra-brauer.
When H⁰(X, O_X) = k this is AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension/picard-brauer-obstruction over T = Spec k.
acceptance: For the pointless real conic X, Pic(X) = 2ℤ ⊂ Pic_{X/ℝ}(ℝ) = ℤ, the cokernel ℤ/2 = Br(ℝ) and n = 2 works.
For X = P¹_ℂ over ℝ, X^aff = Spec ℂ, Br(ℂ) = 0 and Pic(X) = Pic_{X/ℝ}(ℝ) = ℤ.

sources.match: The Leray–Serre sequence for h and G_m gives H¹(X, G_m) → H⁰(S, R¹h_*G_m) → H²(S, h_*G_m) with left arrow the canonical map, and torsion of the right term makes a multiple of every rational point come from an invertible sheaf.
The comparison of Picard functors and the Leray description of the obstruction between Pic(X_T)/Pic(T) and the sheafified Picard functor.

nodes.title: The torsion component Pic^τ_{X/k} is open, closed and of finite type
nodes.statement: Let X be proper over k and G = Pic_{X/k}. Put Pic^τ_{X/k} := ⋃_{n≥1} [n]^{-1}(G⁰), with G⁰ the identity component. Then Pic^τ_{X/k} is an open and closed subgroup scheme of finite type, its formation commutes with every field extension, and for every field K ⊃ k and L ∈ Pic(X_K), the class of L lies in Pic^τ_{X/k}(K) iff L is numerically trivial on X_K. In particular Pic^τ_{X/k}(k̄) = Pic^τ(X_{k̄}/k̄) of NP.0/numerically-trivial (Pic_{X/k}(k̄) = Pic(X_{k̄}) over an algebraically closed field).
hypotheses: X proper over a field; the τ-numerical comparison uses NP.0/field-extension-invariance
proofSteps: G⁰ is an open and closed subgroup of finite type compatible with field extension (group schemes locally of finite type over a field); [n]^{-1}(G⁰) are open and closed subgroups, so G^τ is an open subgroup compatible with field extension (Kleiman, Lemma 6.9).

Over k̄, membership of λ in G^τ is τ-equivalence of L with O_X, which is numerical triviality (Kleiman, Exercise 6.11, Theorem 6.3; for complete X, Remark 6.14 via Chow's lemma and the projection formula).

Quasi-compactness: numerically trivial invertible sheaves on a projective scheme over k̄ form a bounded family (Kleiman, Theorem 6.3 and Proposition 6.12); for proper X pull back to a Chow cover X′ → X, whose induced map on Picard schemes is of finite type (Kleiman, Theorem 4.18.5), so Pic^τ is closed and of finite type. The finite-type relative representability used here is the same deep input left in G4; the proper generality is conditional on it.
Over k̄, every k̄-point of Pic_{X/k} is represented by an invertible sheaf (NP.2/leray-obstruction with Br(X^aff_{k̄}) = 0).
acceptance: Pic^τ_{P¹/k} = 0; for an elliptic curve Pic^τ = Pic⁰ ≅ E; for an Enriques surface over k̄ of characteristic ≠ 2, Pic⁰ = 0 and Pic^τ ≅ ℤ/2.
For an ordinary Enriques surface in characteristic 2, Pic^τ = μ₂ is connected and nonreduced, so Pic^τ = Pic⁰ with its full structure.

sources.locator: Definition 6.8, Lemma 6.9, Exercise 6.11, Proposition 6.12 and Remark 6.14, pp. 56–58
sources.match: G^τ is the union of preimages of G⁰ under the power maps, an open group subscheme compatible with field extension; for the Picard scheme of a complete scheme it is closed of finite type and its points are the τ-equivalent, equivalently numerically trivial, sheaves.
Pic^τ_{X/k} parametrises numerically trivial sheaves, is of finite type and separated, citing SGA 6 Exposé XII Corollary 1.5 and Exposé XIII Theorem 4.7.

nodes.title: The local system of numerical classes Num_{X/k}
nodes.statement: For X proper over a field k put Num_{X/k} := Pic_{X/k}/Pic^τ_{X/k} (fppf quotient). It is an étale group scheme over k, determined by the Galois module Num_{X/k}(k^sep) = Num_{X/k}(k̄) = Num(X_{k̄}/k̄) ≅ ℤ^{ρ} with ρ = ρ(X_{k̄}) ≥ 0, on which Gal(k^sep/k) acts continuously through a finite quotient. The class map Pic(X) → Num(X/k) → Num_{X/k}(k) is injective on Num(X/k).
hypotheses: X proper over a field; ρ = 0 is allowed
proofSteps: Pic^τ_{X/k} is open, so the quotient of the locally finite type group Pic_{X/k} by it is étale (its geometric fibre is the discrete group of components modulo those of Pic^τ).

Over k̄: Num_{X/k}(k̄) = Pic(X_{k̄})/Pic^τ(X_{k̄}/k̄) = Num(X_{k̄}/k̄) by NP.2/tau-component; this is free of finite rank by NP.1/neron-severi-rank. Purely inseparable extensions do not change points of an étale scheme, so the k^sep- and k̄-points agree.
A finitely generated free ℤ-module with continuous action of a profinite group has open stabiliser, so the action factors through a finite quotient.
Injectivity of Num(X/k) → Num_{X/k}(k): if [L] ∈ Pic^τ_{X/k}(k) then L_{k̄} is numerically trivial, hence L is (NP.0/field-extension-invariance).
acceptance: For X geometrically integral with a rational point, Pic(X) → Pic_{X/k}(k) is bijective.

sources.match: Num_{X/k} = Pic_{X/k}/Pic^τ_{X/k} is an étale group scheme, the local system of numerical classes, corresponding to the Galois representation on Num_{X/k}(k^sep) = Num_{X/k}(k^alg) = ℤ^ρ; ρ = 0 occurs; the group schemes exist without reducedness, irreducibility or equidimensionality.

nodes.title: Norms of Picard classes along a finite field extension
nodes.statement: Let E/k be a finite field extension of degree n, X proper over k, pr : X_E → X and q : Spec E → Spec k. For every k-algebra A, pr_A : X_{E⊗A} → X_A is finite locally free of rank n, and the norm of invertible sheaves Nm_{pr_A} : Pic(X_{E⊗A}) → Pic(X_A) (SchemeAndStackFoundations §3.5) is natural in A. It induces a homomorphism of fppf sheaves Nm : q_*Pic_{X_E/E} → Pic_{X/k} with Nm ∘ pr* = [n], mapping q_*Pic^τ_{X_E/E} into Pic^τ_{X/k}.
hypotheses: E/k finite of degree n; X proper over k
proofSteps: The norm along a finite locally free morphism of constant rank n is a homomorphism with Nm(pr*L) ≅ L^{⊗n} and commutes with base change (SchemeAndStackFoundations §3.5); naturality in A passes to fppf sheafifications.
Nm preserves numerical triviality: on a curve C ⊂ X_{K}, deg(Nm L|_C) is a sum of degrees of L on the curves of X_{E⊗K} over C (projection formula), so Nm maps Pic^τ into Pic^τ.
acceptance: For X = P¹_k and E/k of degree n, Nm(O_{P¹_E}(1)) ≅ O_{P¹_k}(n).

nodes.title: Pic^τ-torsors split by a field extension of degree n are killed by n
nodes.statement: Let X be proper over k, P = Pic^τ_{X/k} and l ∈ Num_{X/k}(k). The fibre T_l ⊂ Pic_{X/k} over l is a P-torsor, with class [T_l] ∈ H¹_fppf(k, P). If T_l has a point over a finite extension E/k of degree n, then n·[T_l] = 0; consequently n·l lifts to a k-point of Pic_{X/k}.
hypotheses: X proper over a field; E/k finite of degree n; fppf cohomology
proofSteps: T_l is a P-torsor because Pic → Num is a P-torsor over each point of the étale Num; a closed point of T_l with residue field E splits it over E.
With P_E = P ⊗_k E = Pic^τ_{X_E/E} and q : Spec E → Spec k, the five-term sequence for q gives an injection H¹(k, q_*P_E) → H¹(E, P_E); the class pr*[T_l] maps to the split class, hence is zero.
Apply Nm : q_*P_E → P (NP.2/picard-norm): n·[T_l] = Nm(pr*[T_l]) = 0. A trivial torsor has a rational point, which lifts n·l.
acceptance: For the pointless real conic and l the generator, T_l is split by ℂ and 2l lifts (indeed l itself lifts to Pic_{X/ℝ}(ℝ)).

sources.match: Each rational point of Num is a representable torsor for Pic^τ, trivialised over the residue field of a closed point; the norm and the Leray–Serre sequence show its class has finite order.
The printed vanishing of R¹pr_*P′ is false in general and not needed: injectivity of H¹(k, pr_*P′) → H¹(E, P′) from the five-term sequence suffices.

nodes.title: Positive-power descent criterion for constancy of Num
nodes.statement: Let X be proper over a field k. Num_{X/k} is constant if and only if there is an integer d ≥ 1 such that for every invertible sheaf L on X_{k̄} there is a numerically trivial invertible sheaf N on X_{k̄} with L^{⊗d} ⊗ N isomorphic to the pullback of an invertible sheaf on X.
hypotheses: X proper over a field; d ≥ 1 (d = 0 would make the condition vacuous)
proofSteps: (⇐) The condition says the image of Num(X/k) in Num(X_{k̄}) ≅ ℤ^ρ contains d·ℤ^ρ, which is Galois-fixed; a group acting by automorphisms of a torsion-free ℤ^ρ and fixing d·ℤ^ρ fixes ℤ^ρ.

(⇒) For each l in a basis of Num_{X/k}(k) = ℤ^ρ, NP.2/torsor-torsion gives n ≥ 1 with n·l ∈ image of Pic_{X/k}(k), and NP.2/leray-obstruction gives n′ ≥ 1 with n′n·l ∈ image of Pic(X). Take d the product over a basis; then Pic(X) → Num_{X/k}(k̄) has image containing d·ℤ^ρ.
acceptance: For X = P¹_ℂ over ℝ no d ≥ 1 works (Num not constant), while d = 0 works trivially: this is why d ≥ 1 is required.
For the pointless real conic, d = 2 works and d = 1 does not.

sources.match: Constancy of Num_{X/k} is characterised by the existence of a power d such that every geometric invertible sheaf becomes, up to a numerically trivial twist, a pullback from X after raising to the d-th power; sufficiency by finite index, necessity by torsors and the Leray obstruction.
The printed lemma allows d ≥ 0; with d = 0 the property holds for every X, so d ≥ 1 is required, as the proof uses.

nodes.title: Doubling numerical classes through a 2-torsion kernel
nodes.statement: Let 0 → P → Q → N → 0 be an exact sequence of abelian fppf sheaves (in particular of abelian groups) with 2·P = 0. Multiplication by 2 on Q factors uniquely as d ∘ π for a homomorphism d : N → Q, and π ∘ d = [2]_N. Applied to 0 → Pic^τ_{Y/S} → Pic_{Y/S} → Num_{Y/S} → 0 for a family with 2·Pic^τ = 0 (Enriques families), every section of Num_{Y/S} has a canonical doubled lift to Pic_{Y/S}.
hypotheses: 2·P = 0; exactness in the fppf topology (a sheaf quotient N = Q/P)
proofSteps: [2] : Q → Q kills P, so it factors uniquely through the sheaf quotient N = Q/P; π ∘ d ∘ π = π ∘ [2] = [2] ∘ π, and π is an epimorphism of sheaves.
acceptance: For Q = ℤ/4 ⊃ P = 2ℤ/4, N = ℤ/2 and d(1) = 2.

nodes.title: Finiteness of rational τ-classes over finite fields and torsion over locally finite fields
nodes.statement: (a) For X proper over a finite field F_q, Pic^τ_{X/F_q}(F_{q^r}) is finite for every r ≥ 1. (b) If k is an algebraic extension of a finite field and X is proper over k, every numerically trivial invertible sheaf on X has finite order in Pic(X).

proofSteps: (a) Pic^τ is of finite type over F_q (NP.2/tau-component), so it has finitely many points over each finite field.

(b) X and L are defined over a finite subfield F ⊂ k (spreading out, EGA IV 8.8.2); L₀ on X₀ is numerically trivial (NP.0/field-extension-invariance), so [L₀] ∈ Pic^τ_{X₀/F}(F), a finite group by (a).
Pic(X₀) → Pic_{X₀/F}(F) is injective (NP.2/leray-obstruction), so L₀ has finite order, hence so does L.

nodes.title: Contractions
nodes.statement: A contraction is a proper morphism f : X → Y of schemes for which O_Y → f_*O_X is an isomorphism. In the setting of Schröer, X and Y are proper over a field k; over a Noetherian base S, X and Y are proper S-schemes and f is an S-morphism.
hypotheses: f proper; O_Y ≅ f_*O_X; Y locally Noetherian for the fibre statements
proofSteps: Surjectivity: if y ∉ f(X), then (f_*O_X)_y = 0 ≠ O_{Y,y}.
Geometric connectedness of the fibres is Zariski's connectedness theorem, SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.9 (stein_factorization), for locally Noetherian Y.
Flat base change of f_*O_X (SchemeAndStackFoundations §2.6) shows that contractions are stable under flat base change, in particular under field extension.
acceptance: The blow-up of a regular surface in a closed point is a contraction.
The structure morphism of P¹_ℂ regarded over ℝ is not a contraction to Spec ℝ.

sources.match: A contraction of X is a proper scheme Z with a morphism f : X → Z such that O_Z = f_*(O_X).
Zariski connectedness: a proper morphism of locally Noetherian schemes with O_Z = f_*O_X is surjective with geometrically connected fibres (EGA III 4.3.1, 4.3.4).

nodes.title: Rigidity: maps contracting the curves of a contraction factor through it
nodes.statement: Let S be a Noetherian scheme, f : X → Y a contraction of proper S-schemes and g : X → Z an S-morphism to a scheme Z proper over S. If g maps every integral curve contained in a fibre of f to a point, then there is a unique S-morphism h : Y → Z with g = h ∘ f.
hypotheses: f a contraction; X, Y, Z proper over Noetherian S
proofSteps: Each fibre F = f^{-1}(y) is connected (NP.3/contraction). If g(F) had positive dimension, some integral curve of F would map onto a curve (lift curves as in NP.0/surjective-pullback); so g(F) is finite and connected, a single point.

Let Γ ⊂ Y ×_S Z be the scheme-theoretic image of (f, g). The projection π : Γ → Y is proper with finite fibres, hence finite, and O_Y → π_*O_Γ → f_*O_X = O_Y with the second map injective (Γ is a scheme-theoretic image) forces π_*O_Γ = O_Y, so π is an isomorphism.
h is the second projection composed with π^{-1}; uniqueness holds because f is surjective and O_Y = f_*O_X makes f an epimorphism of schemes.
acceptance: Two contractions X → Y₁, X → Y₂ contracting exactly the same curves are isomorphic under X.
The hypothesis cannot be weakened to a numerical one without the curves: a map contracting fewer curves need not factor.

nodes.title: Semiample invertible sheaves and the section ring
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be proper with S Noetherian. An invertible sheaf L on X is f-semiample if some L^{⊗m}, m ≥ 1, is f-globally generated: f*f_*L^{⊗m} → L^{⊗m} is surjective. Over S = Spec k this is semiampleness (some positive power globally generated). The section ring is R(X/S, L) := ⊕_{t≥0} f_*L^{⊗t}, a quasi-coherent graded O_S-algebra; over a field R(X, L) = ⊕_t H⁰(X, L^{⊗t}) and P(X, L) := Proj R(X, L).
hypotheses: f proper, S Noetherian; m ≥ 1 is required (m = 0 would make every sheaf semiample)
proofSteps: Over a field, global generation descends along every field extension by flat base change of H⁰ and faithful flatness of the evaluation map. Over a general base, fibrewise global generation alone does not imply surjectivity of f*f_*L → L without the appropriate cohomology/base-change hypotheses; no such equivalence is claimed.
A globally generated invertible sheaf has nonnegative degree on every curve (restrict a nonvanishing section at a point of the curve), so semiample sheaves are nef.

nodes.title: Semiample sheaves and projective contractions
nodes.statement: Let X be proper over a field k and L a semiample invertible sheaf. (i) R(X, L) is a finitely generated k-algebra, P(X, L) is projective over k and the canonical morphism φ_L : X → P(X, L) is a contraction; an integral curve C ⊂ X is contracted by φ_L iff (L·C) = 0. (ii) Every contraction f : X → Z with Z projective over k is isomorphic under X to φ_L for L = f*O_Z(1). (iii) R(X, L) and P(X, L) commute with field extension. (iv) If L, L′ are semiample and numerically equivalent, φ_L and φ_{L′} are isomorphic under X.
hypotheses: X proper over a field; L semiample
proofSteps: (i) Choose m with L^{⊗m} globally generated, giving ψ : X → P^N; its Stein factorisation X → Y := Spec_{P^N}(ψ_*O_X) → P^N is a contraction onto a projective Y carrying an ample sheaf whose pullback is L^{⊗m}; the Veronese subring R(X, L^{⊗m}) is the section ring of that ample sheaf, hence finitely generated with Proj equal to Y, and R(X, L) is finite over it, so P(X, L) = Y. Curves with (L·C) = 0 are exactly those mapping to points.
(ii) H⁰(X, f*O_Z(t)) = H⁰(Z, O_Z(t)) by the projection formula and O_Z = f_*O_X, so R(X, f*O(1)) is the section ring of an ample sheaf on Z and Proj of it is Z.
(iii) Flat base change of H⁰ and of Proj.
(iv) φ_L and φ_{L′} contract exactly the curves of degree zero, which are the same curves; by NP.3/rigidity each factors through the other.
acceptance: For L = O_{P¹×P¹}(1, 0), φ_L is the first projection.
For L = O_X, φ_L is X → X^aff.

sources.match: For semiample L, P(X, L) is projective and gives a contraction, each contraction with projective target is of this form, and the sheaf is unique up to pullbacks of semiample sheaves on the target.

hypotheses: X proper over k; Ȳ projective over k̄
proofSteps: k̄ is the filtered union of its finite subextensions; Ȳ, the morphism f̄ and a projective embedding descend to some k′ by EGA IV 8.8.2 (finite presentation) and 8.10.5 (properness, projectivity).
O_{Y′} → f′_*O_{X_{k′}} becomes an isomorphism after the faithfully flat base change to k̄ (flat base change of direct images), hence is one.
acceptance: If f̄ is already defined over k, k′ = k works.

nodes.title: Contractions descend along purely inseparable extensions
nodes.statement: Let k ⊂ k′ be a purely inseparable field extension (possibly infinite), X proper over k and f′ : X_{k′} → Y′ a contraction with Y′ proper over k′ (no projectivity, no condition on Num). There is a contraction f : X → Y over k, with Y proper over k, such that f′ ≅ f_{k′} under X_{k′}.
hypotheses: k′/k purely inseparable; Y′ only proper
proofSteps: pr : X_{k′} → X is a universal homeomorphism (SchemeAndStackFoundations §0.23); put |Y| := |Y′|, f := f′ on spaces and O_Y := f_*O_X, giving a ringed space Y with a morphism X → Y.

Locally: for an affine open V′ ⊂ Y′ with preimage U′ = f′^{-1}(V′) and corresponding U ⊂ X, f′_*O = O makes U′ → V′ = Spec Γ(U′, O) the affine hull; Γ(U′, O) = Γ(U, O) ⊗_k k′ shows U′ → V′ is the base change of U → V = Spec Γ(U, O), and V′ → V is a homeomorphism, so (|V|, O_Y|_{|V|}) ≅ V.
Hence Y is a scheme, Y′ = Y_{k′}, f′ = f_{k′}; Y is proper by fpqc descent of properness along Spec k′ → Spec k (EGA IV 2.7.1).
acceptance: For k′ = k this returns f′.
The statement fails for separable extensions without further hypotheses: contracting one of the two components of (P¹_ℂ)_ℂ = P¹_ℂ ⊔ P¹_ℂ does not descend to ℝ.

In the printed proof the preimage U′ = f′^{-1}(V) should read f′^{-1}(V′), and the continuous map |X′| → |Y′| is f′, not f.

nodes.title: Descent of geometric contractions under constant Num (Schröer, Theorem 1.3)
nodes.statement: Let X be proper over a field k with Num_{X/k} constant. Every contraction f̄ : X_{k̄} → Ȳ with Ȳ projective over k̄ is isomorphic under X_{k̄} to the base change of a contraction f : X → Y over k; Y is then projective over k.
hypotheses: X proper over k; IsConstantNum X; Ȳ projective (the inseparable step alone needs only properness)
proofSteps: Spread the contraction and a projective embedding to a finite normal extension k′/k. Let k₁ be the separable closure of k in k′. Then k₁/k is finite Galois and k′/k₁ is purely inseparable; normality is essential for the cited pinned isGalois instance.

First apply NP.3/inseparable-descent to f′ : X_{k′} → Y′, obtaining f₁ : X_{k₁} → Y₁. The target Y₁ is projective because projectivity descends under a field extension (Stacks Lemma 33.15.5, tag 0BDG). Choose a semiample L₁ defining f₁.

Now take the Galois step over k₁/k: M = ⊗_{σ∈Gal(k₁/k)} σ*L₁ is semiample and numerically equivalent to L₁^{⊗[k₁:k]}; it defines the same contraction by NP.3/semiample-contraction and constancy of Num. Its Picard class is invariant, so is a k-point by Galois descent of the Picard sheaf.

The Leray obstruction is torsion, hence a positive power of this class is represented by an invertible sheaf L on X. Injectivity Pic(X_{k₁}) → Pic_{X/k}(k₁) identifies its pullback with a power of M. Field-extension descent of global generation makes L semiample.

The contraction φ_L has projective target and its base change to k₁, then k′ and k̄, is the prescribed contraction. Averaging a sheaf over k′ before descending the purely inseparable step would not have produced a k₁-point and is not used.
acceptance: For X = P¹_ℂ viewed over ℝ, Num_{X/ℝ} is not constant and the contraction of X_ℂ = P¹_ℂ ⊔ P¹_ℂ collapsing only the first component does not descend.

For X geometrically integral over a finite field with Num constant, every geometric fibration onto a projective curve descends (the Enriques application, EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence Layer 2).

nodes.title: Openness of ampleness for proper algebraic spaces
nodes.statement: Let Y be a Noetherian scheme, f : X → Y a proper morphism from an algebraic space and L an invertible O_X-module. (i) If y ∈ Y is such that the fibre X_y is a scheme and L_y is ample on X_y, there is an open neighbourhood V ∋ y such that L|_{f^{-1}V} is ample on f^{-1}(V)/V; in particular f^{-1}(V) is a scheme, projective over V. (ii) For an arbitrary proper morphism of algebraic spaces f : X → Y there is an open V ⊂ Y such that a morphism Y′ → Y factors through V iff the pullback of L to X ×_Y Y′ is ample over Y′.
hypotheses: (i) Y Noetherian scheme, f proper, X_y a scheme; (ii) f proper morphism of algebraic spaces
proofSteps: (i) Over a Noetherian complete local base the fibrewise very ample powers lift (formal functions, Grothendieck existence), giving a finite morphism to P^r over a neighbourhood after shrinking; a finite morphism to a projective scheme makes X a scheme and L ample. The scheme case of the openness is StableReduction Layer 2's 'fibrewise ample is open'.
(ii) Descent of the ample locus along an étale cover of Y by schemes and the fpqc-local nature of relative ampleness (Stacks 0D2P).
acceptance: For a family of smooth projective curves every fibrewise ample L is relatively ample over the whole base.
Ampleness on one fibre is essential: for the trivial sheaf on X = P¹ × Y, no neighbourhood works.

sources.match: For a proper algebraic space over a Noetherian scheme, if the fibre over y is a scheme on which L is ample, then L is ample over a neighbourhood of y.
For a proper morphism of algebraic spaces there is an open subspace of the target through which a base change factors exactly when the pullback of L is ample.
This openness, with the representability conclusion, is the input of the local projectivity repair of Proposition 5.5; neither R09.1 nor R09.3 names it.

nodes.title: The component dual graph of a Noetherian scheme
nodes.statement: For a Noetherian scheme Z, Γ(Z) is the finite simple graph on its irreducible components; distinct components are adjacent when their intersection is nonempty. A morphism inducing a vertex map must send the closure of the image of each source component onto a target component (or be supplied with such component-dominance data). It sends an edge to an edge or a vertex. Injectivity on vertices gives edge preservation, but even vertex bijectivity does not imply reflection of adjacency for arbitrary morphisms. For field base change, a bijection on vertices does reflect adjacency and gives a graph isomorphism.
hypotheses: Z Noetherian (finitely many components)
proofSteps: Adjacency is symmetric and irreflexive; finiteness of the vertex set is Noetherianity.
If Z′_i ∩ Z′_j ≠ ∅ then their images meet, so adjacent vertices go to adjacent or equal vertices; when the vertex map is injective, equal images cannot occur.

For a field extension K/k, every geometric component dominates a component of Z. If the vertex map is bijective, the support of the pullback of each target component is its unique source component. Faithful flatness preserves nonempty intersections, giving reflection of adjacency.
acceptance: Γ(P¹ ⊔ P¹) has two vertices and no edge; Γ of a nodal cubic is one vertex.

sources.match: The dual graph of a Noetherian scheme has the irreducible components as vertices, joined when they meet; maps sending components to components induce graph morphisms.

The printed claim that such maps send edges to edges fails when two components with the same image meet (x² + y² = 0 over ℝ); edges go to edges or to a vertex, and to edges when the vertex map is bijective.

nodes.title: Constancy of Num for curves is graph descent
nodes.statement: Let X be a proper scheme over k all of whose irreducible components are one-dimensional. Then Num_{X/k} is constant iff Γ(X_{k̄}) → Γ(X) is a graph isomorphism.
hypotheses: X proper over k; every irreducible component of dimension one (zero-dimensional components excluded)
proofSteps: An invertible sheaf is numerically trivial iff its degrees on the reduced components C_1, …, C_r vanish, so Num(X_{k̄}) ⊗ ℚ has the components of X_{k̄} as a dual basis.

(⇐) If the vertex map is bijective, choose closed points a_i in C_i outside the other components and outside the embedded points, and effective Cartier divisors D_i supported at a_i; the classes of O(D_i) span a finite-index subgroup of Num_{X/k}(k̄) defined over k, so Galois acts trivially (NP.2/positive-power-criterion).

(⇒) For a component E of X_{k̄}, take an effective Cartier divisor on X_{k̄} supported on E away from the others; NP.2/positive-power-criterion gives L on X with (L_{k̄}·E′) ≥ 0, positive exactly for E′ = E, so exactly one component of X lies under E: the vertex map is bijective.
acceptance: For X = P¹_ℂ viewed over ℝ, Γ(X_ℂ) has two vertices over one: Num is not constant.
For X = P¹_ℝ ⊔ Spec ℂ the statement is outside the hypothesis: Num_{X/ℝ} = ℤ is constant but Γ(X_ℂ) has three vertices over two.

nodes.title: Intersection matrices and intersection-labelled graphs of curves on a surface
nodes.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k with H⁰(S, O_S) = k and C ⊂ S a curve with irreducible components C_1, …, C_r and multiplicities m_i ≥ 1. Its intersection matrix is N(C) := ((C_i·C_j))_{i,j} ∈ Mat_r(ℤ), intersection numbers on S over k (SchemeAndStackFoundations §5.9). C is negative definite (resp. negative semidefinite) if N(C) is. The labelled graph of C is Γ(C) with each edge {C_i, C_j}, i ≠ j, labelled by (C_i·C_j) > 0.
hypotheses: S smooth proper over k with H⁰(S, O_S) = k; intersection numbers over k
proofSteps: Distinct components meet iff (C_i·C_j) > 0 (local intersection multiplicities are positive at common points), so labels are positive exactly on edges.
N(C) is symmetric by symmetry of the intersection pairing.
acceptance: For two lines in P²_k, N = [[1,1],[1,1]].

nodes.title: Contractions of smooth proper surfaces
nodes.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k with H⁰(S, O_S) = k and f : S → Z a contraction. Exactly one of the following holds: (a) Z = Spec k and f is the structure morphism; (b) Z is a geometrically normal proper surface and f is birational; (c) Z is a smooth proper geometrically connected curve over k, and f is flat with geometrically connected fibres (f is of fibre type).
hypotheses: S smooth proper surface, H⁰(S, O_S) = k; f a contraction
proofSteps: Z is normal and, after the flat base change to k̄, geometrically normal: O_Z = f_*O_S with S normal, and contractions commute with field extension (NP.3/contraction).
dim Z = 0: Z = Spec H⁰(Z, O_Z) = Spec H⁰(S, O_S) = Spec k.
dim Z = 2: f is generically finite, and O_Z = f_*O_S forces the generic fibre to have degree one, so f is birational.

dim Z = 1: a geometrically normal curve is smooth; S is integral and dominates the Dedekind scheme Z, so f is flat; H⁰(Z, O_Z) = k with Z geometrically reduced gives geometric connectedness; fibres are geometrically connected by Zariski connectedness.
acceptance: The blow-up of P²_k at a k-point is of type (b); P¹×P¹ → P¹ is of type (c); S → Spec k is of type (a).

The printed dichotomy omits the contraction to Spec k; Theorem 2.1 excludes it by assuming one-dimensional geometric fibres.

nodes.title: Negative definiteness of exceptional curves (Du Val, Mumford, Grauert)
nodes.statement: Let S be a regular two-dimensional scheme, proper over a field k, f : S → Z a proper birational morphism onto a normal surface and z ∈ Z a closed point with dim f^{-1}(z) = 1. The irreducible components E_1, …, E_r of f^{-1}(z) have negative definite intersection matrix ((E_i·E_j)). For the base-change application assume additionally that S is smooth over k and Z is geometrically normal; then after any algebraically closed extension Ω/k the theorem applies to the closed fibre points of f_Ω. Regularity alone need not survive a field extension.
hypotheses: S regular, f proper birational onto a normal surface; intersection numbers over k (any positive rescaling preserves definiteness)
proofSteps: Localise at z: X = S ×_Z Spec O_{Z,z} → Spec O_{Z,z} is a desingularisation of a two-dimensional normal local ring.

Choose a nonunit r ∈ O_{Z,z}; its pullback divisor C = Σ c_iE_i + (strict part) satisfies (C·E_i) = 0 for all i, with c_i > 0 by connectedness of the fibre (Zariski) and the strict part meeting some E_i; the standard criterion then gives definiteness.

For the geometric application use smoothness of S and geometric normality of Z, so S_Ω is regular and Z_Ω is normal. Flat base change preserves the contraction, and birationality persists for these geometrically integral surfaces. Do not base change a merely regular surface without this additional hypothesis.
acceptance: For the blow-up of a point, ((E·E)) = (−1).
For the minimal resolution of an A_n singularity, the matrix is the negative of the A_n Cartan matrix.

sources.match: For a desingularisation of a two-dimensional normal local ring, the intersection matrix of the components of the closed fibre is negative definite (a lemma of Du Val).
Cites Mumford 1961 for negative definiteness of the intersection form on exceptional curves of a birational morphism of surfaces.
Negativity of exceptional curves is the birational case of Theorem 2.1, applied after base change to Ω.

nodes.title: Zariski's lemma for fibres of fibrations of regular surfaces
nodes.statement: Let S be a regular two-dimensional scheme, f : S → Z a proper flat morphism onto a regular one-dimensional scheme with O_Z = f_*O_S, z ∈ Z a closed point and f^*(z) = Σ_{i=1}^r m_iC_i its fibre. Then (C_i·C_j) ≥ 0 for i ≠ j, with equality iff C_i ∩ C_j = ∅; (f^*(z)·C_j) = 0 for all j; the intersection form on ⊕ℚC_i is negative semidefinite with radical ℚ·Σm_iC_i; every proper subset of {C_1, …, C_r} spans a negative definite sublattice; in particular C_i² < 0 for every i when r ≥ 2.
hypotheses: S regular of dimension two; f proper flat with connected fibres onto a regular curve; no smoothness of the generic fibre is needed
proofSteps: Localise at z to get a regular proper flat model over the discrete valuation ring O_{Z,z}; the special fibre is connected because O_Z = f_*O_S.

(C_i·C_j) ≥ 0 for i ≠ j from local intersection multiplicities; (f^*(z)·C_j) = 0 because f^*(z) is the divisor of a uniformiser; no proper nonempty subset is orthogonal to its complement, by connectedness.

The matrix conclusion is already proved in current Tau Ceti, Matrix.dotProduct_mulVec_nonpos_of_mulVec_eq_zero and Matrix.dotProduct_mulVec_eq_zero_iff_of_mulVec_eq_zero (LinearAlgebra/Matrix/NegSemidef.lean), with the proper-principal-submatrix form TauCeti.NumericalType.sum_sum_intersection_mul_neg (Curves/StableReduction/NumericalType/IntersectionForm.lean). Import that linear algebra; the new step here is its geometric application to regular proper flat models without a smooth generic fibre. Inspection of Stacks Lemma 55.9.7 shows that its proof uses only positivity, the multiplicity relation and connectedness.
acceptance: For a fibre of type I₂ (two rational curves meeting in two points), N = [[−2, 2], [2, −2]].
For an irreducible fibre, N = [0].

nodes.title: Descent of curves with negative self-intersection
nodes.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k and Ω/k an algebraically closed extension. A reduced integral curve C ⊂ S_Ω with C² < 0 is defined over a finite separable extension of k. If Num_{S/k} is constant, C = D_Ω for a geometrically integral curve D ⊂ S defined over k.
hypotheses: S smooth and proper over k; Ω algebraically closed over k; C a reduced integral curve on S_Ω with negative self-intersection; constancy of Num only for the final assertion
proofSteps: Use the Hilbert algebraic space of proper subschemes of S (Stacks Proposition 99.9.4). At [C] its tangent space is Hom(I_C,O_C) = H⁰(C,O_C(C)), by the quotient-deformation formula of Remark 99.7.10; C is Cartier because S_Ω is regular.

The normal line bundle has degree C² < 0 on an integral proper curve, hence has no nonzero global section. The Hilbert space is locally of finite presentation and has zero geometric tangent space here, so it is unramified at [C]. Over a field it is flat, hence étale there. Such a point has a finite separable field of definition, even if Ω/k is transcendental.

Choose a finite Galois extension defining C. Constancy of Num makes its conjugates numerically equal: after an algebraically closed extension the lattice is unchanged, and its Galois action is trivial. Two distinct effective integral curves have nonnegative mutual intersection, whereas numerical equality would make their mutual intersection equal to C² < 0. Thus every conjugate equals C.

Galois descent of the closed subscheme gives D over k; its base change to Ω is integral and reduced, so D is geometrically integral. This proves a stronger field-of-definition statement than the residue conclusion of SCH23; it is an independent repair, not a quotation of its proof.
acceptance: An exceptional (−1)-curve on a smooth surface with constant Num is defined over k.
On a real quadric whose two rulings are conjugate, a ruling has square zero; the negative hypothesis cannot be dropped.
On the blow-up of P²_ℝ at a nonreal closed point, the two geometric exceptional curves are conjugate and Num is not constant.

sources.match: The separated finite-presentation Hilbert functor is an algebraic space locally of finite presentation, and first-order quotient deformations are controlled by Hom from the kernel to the quotient. The negative-curve descent argument above is an application of these results.

nodes.title: Descent of fibre dual graphs under constant Num (Schröer, Theorem 2.1(i))
nodes.statement: Let S be a smooth proper surface over k with H⁰(S, O_S) = k and Num_{S/k} constant, f : S → Z a contraction, ā : Spec Ω → Z a geometric point with image a, S_ā = S ×_Z Spec Ω and S_a = f^{-1}(a). If S_ā is one-dimensional, then Γ(S_ā) → Γ(S_a) is a graph isomorphism.
hypotheses: S smooth proper, H⁰(S, O_S) = k, Num_{S/k} constant; S_ā one-dimensional (so f is birational or of fibre type)
proofSteps: Work over an algebraically closed Ω containing κ(a); the geometric fibre is a closed curve on S_Ω. Apply the surface-contraction trichotomy after this base change.

If the fibre has at least two components, every component has negative self-intersection, by exceptional negativity in the birational case or Zariski’s lemma in the fibre-type case. NP.4/negative-curve-descent therefore defines each component over k. If it has one component, the vertex map is automatically bijective.

In the reducible case the descended k-curves give distinct components over κ(a), so the vertex map is bijective. For field base change, vertex bijectivity preserves and reflects intersections (NP.4/component-dual-graph), giving the graph isomorphism. The Hilbert input used for this repair remains G5.
acceptance: Over a finite field, every geometrically reducible fibre of a genus-one fibration of an Enriques surface with constant Num has its geometric components defined over its residue field (EnriquesSurfacesAndIntegralNonexistence 2.19).

Without constant Num the statement fails: for a conic bundle S → P¹_ℝ with a fibre x² + y² = 0 over a real point a, Γ(S_ā) has two vertices (the conjugate lines) over one vertex of Γ(S_a), and complex conjugation swaps their classes in Num(S_ℂ).

sources.match: With Num constant, the geometric-to-schematic fibre graph map is an isomorphism: negative definiteness (birational case) or semidefiniteness (fibre type) makes the components numerically independent, so Galois fixes them.
In the fibre-type case the printed use of the two subcurves C₁+…+C_{r−1} and C₂+…+C_r does not exclude C₁ and C_r being exchanged; the one-line fix (C_i − C_j)·C_i < 0 separates all classes.

nodes.title: Residue fields of reducible geometric fibres are purely inseparable (Theorem 2.1(iii))
nodes.statement: In the situation of NP.4/fibre-graph-descent, if S_ā is reducible then a is a closed k-rational point: κ(a) = k. In particular the purely inseparable conclusion of SCH23 Theorem 2.1(iii) holds. The stronger conclusion here uses NP.4/negative-curve-descent and its explicit Hilbert-space prerequisite G5.
hypotheses: as in NP.4/fibre-graph-descent, with S_ā reducible
proofSteps: A geometric fibre with at least two components has a component C of negative self-intersection, as in NP.4/fibre-graph-descent. Descend it to a geometrically integral proper curve D over k by NP.4/negative-curve-descent.

The restriction f|_D becomes a constant morphism after the faithfully flat extension to Ω. Its scheme-theoretic image W is proper over k and has W_Ω a single reduced Ω-point; hence W = Spec k by descent. The geometric image point lies over a, so a is closed with κ(a)=k. Equivalently, after knowing the image is a closed point, κ(a) embeds in H⁰(D,O_D)=k.

This also handles geometric points lying over a nonclosed point of Z: a reducible fibre there would force that point to be closed, a contradiction. There is no assumption that κ(a)/k was finite before proving it.
acceptance: Over a finite field every purely inseparable extension is trivial, so reducible geometric fibres lie over rational points.

sources.match: If the geometric fibre is reducible, the residue extension k ⊂ κ(a) is purely inseparable, since otherwise Galois would permute the components of S_a ⊗_k Ω nontrivially.

nodes.title: Edge labels of fibre graphs descend (Theorem 2.1(ii), corrected)
nodes.statement: In the situation of NP.4/fibre-graph-descent, suppose S_ā is reducible and (S_a)_red is geometrically reduced over κ(a). Then κ(a) = k, and the graph isomorphism Γ(S_ā) → Γ(S_a) preserves edge labels: (C_i·C_j) on S_Ω equals (D_i·D_j) on S for the components C_i, C_j of S_ā over the components D_i, D_j of S_a. When the geometric fibre has only one component, label preservation is vacuous; the residue-field assertion here is only for reducible fibres.
hypotheses: as in NP.4/fibre-graph-descent; S_ā reducible; (S_a)_red geometrically reduced over κ(a)
proofSteps: With one component there are no edges and hence no labels to compare. Treat the reducible case for the substantive assertion below.

NP.4/reducible-fibre-residue now gives a closed point a with κ(a)=k, by the negative-curve Hilbert rigidity argument. This step depends on G5, and is stronger than the statement printed as Theorem 2.1(iii).

Each geometric component C_i descends to a geometrically integral divisor D_i on S by NP.4/negative-curve-descent. Thus the full Cartier pullback is D_{i,Ω}=C_i, without a nilpotent multiplicity. Proper intersection numbers are invariant under field extension, so (D_i·D_j)_k=(C_i·C_j)_Ω.

This proves the source’s label assertion under its stated geometric-reducedness hypothesis (in fact the repair proves geometric integrality of the components). No comparison between q and q² is used: the old q-scaling formula for a fibre inside S was unjustified.
acceptance: Over a finite field the residue extension is trivial by (iii) and the labels agree directly.

sources.match: The graph isomorphism respects edge labels provided the reduced schematic fibre is geometrically reduced over the residue field; the proof is left to the reader.

nodes.title: Restriction of numerical classes to the special fibre over a DVR
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with residue field k, S = Spec R, and 𝒳 → S proper with special fibre X = 𝒳 ⊗_R k. The curves over S are exactly the integral curves of X, so N₁(𝒳/S) is a quotient of N₁(X/k), and restriction of invertible sheaves induces res : N¹(𝒳/S) → N¹(X/k), [𝓛] ↦ [𝓛|_X], which is injective. 𝒳/S is called numerically surjective when res is surjective (equivalently its ℚ-form is).
hypotheses: R a DVR; 𝒳 → Spec R proper (projective in the sources)
proofSteps: The only closed point of S is the closed point, so by NP.0/closed-points-suffice 𝓛 ≡_S 0 iff 𝓛|_X ≡ 0: res is well defined and injective.
A 1-cycle on X pairs with Pic(𝒳) through restriction; it is numerically trivial on 𝒳/S iff it annihilates the image of res, so N₁(𝒳/S) = N₁(X)/(image of res)^⊥.
acceptance: For 𝒳 = P^n_R, res : ℝ → ℝ is the identity on the degree.

sources.locator: Theorem 1.3(2), p. 2, and the remark after Theorem 1.4, p. 3
sources.match: The hypothesis that N¹(𝒳/Spec R) → N¹(X) is surjective for a lift over a DVR, with N¹ = Pic ⊗ ℚ modulo numerical equivalence; completeness of R is needed for surjectivity via Lemma 6.3.
Only curves projective over S, hence lying in the special fibre, enter NE(𝒳/S); numerical relations on 𝒳 and X agree when the restriction is surjective.

nodes.title: Numerical surjectivity gives numerical, not actual, lifts
nodes.statement: In the situation of NP.5/special-fibre-restriction, assume 𝒳/S is numerically surjective. Then for every L ∈ Pic(X) there are m ≥ 1 and 𝓛 ∈ Pic(𝒳) with 𝓛|_X ≡ L^{⊗m} (numerical equivalence on X); equivalently every ℚ-line bundle on X is numerically the restriction of a ℚ-Cartier class on 𝒳. Numerical surjectivity does not imply that L itself, is isomorphic to the restriction of an invertible sheaf on 𝒳. This assertion does not claim that every positive power also fails to lift.
hypotheses: R a DVR, 𝒳/S proper and numerically surjective
proofSteps: Num(𝒳/S) and Num(X) are lattices of the same rank in N¹ (NP.1/finite-dimensionality), and res maps the first injectively into the second with finite index when surjective after ⊗ℚ; m can be taken to be that index.

For the exact-lift distinction take the smooth proper model over ℤ_(7) of E : y²+y=x³−x²−10x−20 (Cremona 11a1, LMFDB 11.a2). Its rational group is ℤ/5 and its F₇-group has 10 points (direct enumeration gives 9 affine points and infinity). Every generic line bundle extends across this regular model, and a vertical divisor is a multiple of the principal special fibre, so Pic(𝒳)=Pic(E_ℚ). Thus a degree-zero special class outside the image of E(ℚ) does not lift exactly, although it is numerically lifted by O. Every degree-zero special class is torsion, so a positive power is trivial and does lift; this example cannot support the old stronger claim.
acceptance: When H²(X, O_X) = 0 and R is complete, actual lifts exist (NP.5/line-bundle-lifting).

nodes.title: Line bundles lift over a complete DVR when H²(X, O_X) = 0
nodes.statement: Let R be a complete discrete valuation ring, 𝒳 → Spec R proper flat with special fibre X, and H²(X, O_X) = 0. Every invertible sheaf L on X is isomorphic to 𝓛|_X for some invertible 𝓛 on 𝒳; in particular 𝒳/R is numerically surjective. If L is ample, every such 𝓛 is ample over R.
hypotheses: R complete DVR (any characteristics); 𝒳 proper flat over R; H²(X, O_X) = 0
proofSteps: Lift L successively to X_n = 𝒳 ⊗ R/m^{n+1}: the obstruction lies in H²(X, O_X) ⊗ m^n/m^{n+1} = 0 (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry A0-extension/picard-infinitesimal-lifting, framed lifts along the flat thickenings).
Grothendieck's existence theorem (SchemeAndStackFoundations §4.10) algebraises the compatible system (L_n) to an invertible 𝓛 on 𝒳 with 𝓛|_X ≅ L.

Ampleness: the closed fibre is the only fibre over a closed point, so openness of ampleness (NP.3/ampleness-openness, scheme case) makes 𝓛 ample over a neighbourhood of the closed point, which is all of Spec R.
acceptance: For a lift of a curve (H² = 0 automatically), every line bundle lifts; for a lift of an abelian or K3 surface the hypothesis fails and the Picard rank can drop.

sources.match: For a complete mixed-characteristic DVR and a lift of X with H²(X, O_X) = 0, every line bundle lifts (obstructions in H², Grothendieck existence), so N¹(𝒳/R) → N¹(X) is surjective, and ample lifts are ample by Stacks 0D3A; the argument does not use the characteristic.
Infinitesimal lifting of invertible sheaves has obstruction in H²(X, O_X).

nodes.title: Numerical surjectivity identifies relative and special-fibre cones
nodes.statement: In the situation of NP.5/special-fibre-restriction, if 𝒳/S is numerically surjective then res : N¹(𝒳/S) → N¹(X) is an isomorphism, the identity on cycles induces N₁(X) ≅ N₁(𝒳/S), and under these identifications NE‾(𝒳/S) = NE‾(X), Nef(𝒳/S) = Nef(X), and extremal rays and faces of the two cones correspond. A class on 𝒳 is relatively ample over S iff its restriction to X is ample.
hypotheses: R a DVR; 𝒳/S proper and numerically surjective
proofSteps: res is injective (NP.5/special-fibre-restriction) and surjective by hypothesis; dualising gives N₁(X) ≅ N₁(𝒳/S) because the curves are the same and the annihilator of im res is zero.
Effective cycles correspond under the identity, so the cones and their closures agree; nef cones are their duals; faces correspond.
Ampleness over S is tested on the special fibre by openness of ampleness (NP.3/ampleness-openness).
acceptance: For 𝒳 = P^n_R both cones are the ray of a line.

sources.match: When N¹(𝒳/S) → N¹(X) is surjective, NE(𝒳/S) = NE(X), because only curves in the special fibre enter and numerical relations agree; an extremal ray of X is cut out on 𝒳 by a lifted ample class.

nodes.title: Nef and big classes on the special fibre are nef and big on the generic fibre
nodes.statement: Let R be a DVR and T → Spec R flat and projective with integral special fibre T_s and integral generic fibre T_η of dimension n ≥ 1, and let H be a ℚ-Cartier divisor on T. If H|_{T_s} is nef and big then H|_{T_η} is nef and big. The conclusion depends only on the numerical class of H|_{T_s}.
hypotheses: R a DVR; T → Spec R flat projective with integral fibres of dimension n; H ℚ-Cartier on T
proofSteps: Top self-intersections are constant in flat proper families: χ(T_t, mH|_{T_t}) is independent of t, and (H_t^n) is n! times its leading coefficient in m; so (H_η^n) = (H_s^n) > 0.
Nefness: for an integral curve C_η ⊂ T_η, its closure 𝒞 ⊂ T is flat over R and its special fibre is an effective 1-cycle Σ a_iC_i on T_s; constancy of χ on 𝒞 gives (H·C_η) = Σ a_i (H·C_i) ≥ 0.

Apply the projective nef-and-big criterion imported by NP.1/big from SF.5/nef-big-numerical: both fibres here are projective, so G3 (the arbitrary proper extension) is not used. Nefness and the top self-intersection depend only on numerical classes.
acceptance: For T = P^n_R and H = O(1), both restrictions are ample.

The converse fails even with smooth integral fibres. Over k[[t]], blow up P² along the three disjoint sections [1:0:0], [0:1:0], [1:1:t]. For H=2h−e₁−e₂−e₃, the generic three points are noncollinear, so H is nef and H²=1. On the special fibre their common line has strict transform ℓ=h−e₁−e₂−e₃ and H·ℓ=−1. The family and both fibres are smooth; the counterexample is not a blow-up confined to a special point.

sources.match: For a flat projective family over a DVR with integral three-dimensional fibres, a ℚ-Cartier H whose special restriction is nef and big has nef and big generic restriction, independently of the numerical representative; supplied in the extraction for the repaired proof of the published Theorem 6.1(2b).
Top self-intersections of K + tA agree on the generic and special fibres of the lift, which is used to compare bigness.

nodes.title: Relatively semiample, relatively numerically trivial sheaves descend
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Z be a contraction of schemes proper over a Noetherian scheme S, and L an invertible sheaf on X that is f-semiample and f-numerically trivial. Then there are m ≥ 1 and an invertible sheaf M on Z with L^{⊗m} ≅ f*M. For ℚ-Cartier divisors: an f-semiample, f-numerically trivial ℚ-Cartier D on X is ℚ-linearly equivalent to f* of a ℚ-Cartier divisor on Z.
hypotheses: f a contraction; L f-semiample and ≡_f 0
proofSteps: Choose m with f*f_*L^{⊗m} → L^{⊗m} surjective; it defines a Z-morphism φ : X → P = P_Z(f_*L^{⊗m}) with L^{⊗m} ≅ φ*O_P(1).
Since L ≡_f 0, φ maps every curve in a fibre of f to a point (O_P(1) is ample on the fibres of P → Z); by NP.3/rigidity φ = h ∘ f for a unique Z-morphism h : Z → P.
Then L^{⊗m} ≅ f*(h*O_P(1)); put M := h*O_P(1).
acceptance: For f the structure map X → X^aff of a proper k-scheme and L torsion, the conclusion holds with M trivial on the finite X^aff.
Semiampleness cannot be dropped: on an elliptic curve E → Spec k, O(p − q) of infinite order is numerically trivial and no power is pulled back from the point.

sources.match: For the semiample fibration of a nef L, every relatively numerically trivial ℚ-Cartier divisor descends; the proof makes L + D semiample over the base and descends it.
In the contraction of an extremal face, numerically trivial ℚ-Cartier divisors over Z descend to Z.

nodes.title: Vertical numerical descent (Cascini–Tanaka, Lemma 2.17)
nodes.statement: Let f : X → S be a proper morphism of integral normal excellent schemes with f_*O_X = O_S, and L a ℚ-Cartier ℚ-divisor on X. Assume S is ℚ-factorial, L is f-nef, L restricted to the generic fibre X_{K(S)} is ℚ-linearly trivial, and every prime divisor D of X has f(D) equal to S or to a prime divisor of S. Then L ∼_ℚ f*M for a ℚ-Cartier ℚ-divisor M on S.
hypotheses: f proper, X, S integral normal excellent, f_*O_X = O_S; S ℚ-factorial; L f-nef, generically ℚ-trivial; no prime divisor of X maps to a closed subset of codimension ≥ 2
proofSteps: Replace L by a Cartier multiple; generic ℚ-triviality gives mL + div(φ) = L′ with Supp L′ ⊂ f^{-1}(S₀), S₀ ⊊ S closed.

By hypothesis every component of L′ maps onto a prime divisor P of S; ℚ-factoriality makes f*P a ℚ-Cartier divisor, and subtracting a multiple of f*P makes L′ ≤ 0 over the generic point of P with one coefficient zero.

The needed local step is vertical negativity: over O_{S,P}, an f-nef vertical divisor which is nonpositive and has a zero coefficient must vanish. CT20 invokes this via cuts to surface models. The surface matrix result alone does not supply the cuts in the excellent generality stated here; this exact input is G6, so this proof stops conditionally at that step. Once it is supplied, remove one P at a time and descend the resulting divisor from S.
acceptance: For f a projective bundle over a regular S, every f-nef L trivial on the generic fibre is a pullback.

The last hypothesis is needed: for the blow-up f : X = Bl_p S → S of a closed point on a regular surface, L = O(−E) is f-nef ((−E)·E = 1), trivial on the generic fibre, and not ℚ-linearly a pullback since pullbacks have degree 0 on E; here E maps to a point.

nodes.title: Extremal curves of minimal normalised degree on a ray
nodes.statement: Let f : X → T be projective with T Noetherian, R ⊂ NE‾(X/T) a ray containing the class of some curve over T, and H an f-ample Cartier divisor. For curves C over T with [C] ∈ R, the numbers (H·C)/d_C are positive integers, where d_C is the curve index of C over the residue field of its image point (NP.0/curve-index). Hence the minimum μ_H(R) = min{(H·C)/d_C : [C] ∈ R} is attained; a curve attaining it is called extremal. Extremality does not depend on H, and for every ℚ-Cartier D with D·R < 0, an extremal Γ maximises (D·C)/d_C among curves in R.
hypotheses: f projective, T Noetherian; R a ray spanned by a curve class
proofSteps: d_C divides (H·C) (NP.0/curve-index), and (H·C) > 0 for f-ample H, so (H·C)/d_C ∈ ℤ_{>0}; a nonempty set of positive integers has a minimum.
All curves in R have classes λ_C·ξ for a fixed generator ξ with λ_C > 0; for another ample H′, (H·C)/(H′·C) = (H·ξ)/(H′·ξ) is constant on R, so the minimisers coincide.
For D·R < 0, (D·C)/d_C = λ_C(D·ξ)/d_C with D·ξ < 0 is maximal exactly where λ_C/d_C, equivalently (H·C)/d_C, is minimal.
acceptance: On P^n_k over k the lines are extremal, with (O(1)·line)/d = 1.
For X = P¹_ℂ viewed over T = Spec ℝ, d_X = 2 and (O(1)·X)_ℝ/d_X = 1.

sources.match: A curve Γ in an extremal ray is extremal if it minimises H·C/d_C; the notion is independent of the ample H, and negative divisors on the ray are maximised by it.

nodes.title: The Alexeev–Hacon–Kawamata birational Picard rank
nodes.statement: Let Y be a normal projective variety over ℂ and π : X → Y a projective resolution with X smooth. Define ρ_AHK(Y) := ρ(X) − #{π-exceptional prime divisors}. This integer is independent of resolution, is invariant under birational maps that are isomorphisms in codimension one, and agrees with ρ(Y) when Y is ℚ-factorial. It is not in general the rank of Cartier numerical classes on a singular Y. A relative version over a Noetherian base, particularly in positive characteristic as used by HW23, is a separate remaining target G7; it is not asserted from AHK07 Lemma 1.6.
hypotheses: Normal projective complex variety Y; projective smooth resolutions and common dominating resolutions (the setting of AHK07, p. 1 and Lemma 1.6).
proofSteps: AHK Lemma 1.6 proves independence of exceptional divisor classes by cutting to regular surfaces and using their negative intersection form. In its dimension count the number of extra hyperplanes on X must be dim X−e−2, after e cuts on Y, rather than the printed dim X−e+2.

For a birational morphism g : X₃ → X₁ of smooth projective varieties, pushforward and pullback of Cartier divisors split their classes modulo the independent exceptional divisors. Hence ρ(X₃)=ρ(X₁)+#Exc(g). A common smooth resolution compares any two resolutions of Y.

Small birational modifications have the same exceptional prime divisors on a common resolution. If Y is ℚ-factorial, every pushed-forward Weil divisor has a Cartier multiple; this identifies the quotient by exceptional classes with N¹(Y).

These arguments use projective complex hyperplane sections and smooth resolutions. HW23 p. 12 uses a relative positive-characteristic analogue but does not prove the extra hyperplane, regularity and numerical-independence inputs; these are requested in G7 before that application is closed.
